To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the DNA release from its complexation with a cationic lipid is due to ion-pairing between cationic lipid and anionic additives.
DNA upon binding with a number of positively charged lipids becomes resistant to nuklease digestion, loses its ability to intercalates, and becomes less mobile in aqueous medium.

the release of DNA from its complex with cationic lipid could be induced by anions through the interlipidic interaction, the ion-pair formation between cationic lipid and the anionic amphiphilic additives.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanistic aspects of DNA release from cations amphiphile-DMA complexes.
the mechanism of DNA delivery by cationic amphipathic molecules and the role of the lipid moiety in this process.
the elucidation of molecular mechanisms of transfection by cationic amphipathic molecules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the DNA release from cations amphiphile-DNAs complexes could be induced with several anionic additives, which is most effective when the ion-pair formation between anionic and cationic amphipathic molecules occurs in a thermodynamically favorable way.

cationic lipid-induced DNA condensation and release of DNA from its complex with cationic lipid are the result of a balance between electrostatic forces and hydrophobic and ion-pairing interactions between cation- and anionic amphipaths.
DNA gets complexed with the cationic amphipathic lipid in the lamellar phase and the complexation is most efficient when the complexation is performed at or near the Tm of cationic lipid.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DNA release from the cation-lipid-DNA complex by anions is due to the ion-paired formation of cationic and amphiphiles.

DNA is released from its complexes by the anionic amphiphilic additives through ion-pairing with cationic lipid molecules, the melting profile of which is similar to that of the cation alone in the absence of anion, DNA, and water.
the cationic liposome-DNA complexation and the release of DNA from the complexes are driven by electrostatic forces, hydrophobic interactions, and ion-pairing between the amphiphiles involved.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DNA is released from the cation lipid-DNA complex by the anion-induced ion-pairing between anionic and cationic amphiphs.
the DNA release from the lipid-DNA complex can be induced by anion-mediated ion-pairing between the anionic and cationic amphipathic molecules.

the release of DNA from its complexes with the cationic liposome could be induced by anion-induced ion-pairing between cationic liposomal components and anion-induced disruption of the lamellar organization in the cation lipid-DNA complex.
